parsed.explanation: The combined regime layers a hostile federal document/entry regime (X-marker bar, M/F-only processing upheld by the Supreme Court, visa case-note tag with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility, federally funded single-sex facility bans) onto a division with birth-certificate bathroom mandates extending to colleges, an ID surgery requirement upheld through 2024, no statewide nondiscrimination or GI hate-crime coverage, and a documented restroom arrest with 24-hour men's-ward holding. Documented immigration-custody abuse (beatings, solitary, sexual abuse of trans detainees) is state-perpetrated severity-4 exposure reachable by a traveller refused entry. No criminalisation of trans identity itself, marriage equality, national employment and hate-crime protections, and functioning (if hostile) courts cap the score well above the criminalisation tier.

entry_documents.exposure: Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where documents cast doubt on sex and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility; foreign governments issued travel advisories; passport-marker regime blocks M/F/X congruence for US-issued documents; division requires surgery for marker change, so daily ID mismatch is common.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid until expiry; fraud finding requires four elements, is never automatic, with limited waiver; litigation pending before a civil-liberties union suit.
entry_documents.interaction: Document mismatch at entry can escalate: secondary screening → refusal → immigration custody, where documented trans detainee abuse applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Immigration custody documents forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement and severe sexual abuse of trans men, with guard statements justifying mistreatment; corrections bureau adopted conversion-therapy-style policies from 2026 and stopped reporting trans prisoner counts; division documented a 24-hour men's-ward hold after a restroom arrest.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; formal charging, bail and counsel procedures exist; several executive orders enjoined or blocked in court.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry refusal or document discrepancy routes the traveller into the same federal custody system where abuse is documented; hostile institutional policy is the enforced practice, so functioning procedure does not mitigate.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Universal-exposure tier 1: federal order bars trans people from federally funded single-sex facilities; division HB322 mandates birth-certificate bathrooms in schools, college bans enacted per 2026 assessment, SB79 declares binary gender (Feb 2025); 4 divisions criminalise certain facility use, with a documented 2025 trespass arrest and handcuffing.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 divisions plus capital district lack mapped bans; 6-division private-setting scope limited; trespass requires willful entry plus refusal to leave, with exemptions.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Facility rules bite travellers in public buildings, transport hubs and any school/college-affiliated site visited; arrest risk converts a universal exposure into custody.

care_services.exposure: No statewide nondiscrimination in public accommodations or insurance, no ban on insurance exclusions — a traveller can be denied service or care; division criminalises provision of gender-affirming care to under-19s (Class C felony, 10 years), directly endangering an adult travelling with a minor seeking such care; DOJ subpoenaed hospital records for under-19s nationally.
care_services.protection: Emergency-care duty and employment nondiscrimination under the 2020 ruling persist; litigation pending against the Oct 2025 proposed rules.
care_services.interaction: A visiting parent accompanying a trans minor risks both care refusal and, if care is sought, exposure of clinicians to felony liability that chills treatment; national and division rules compound.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive orders label care 'malignation', direct law enforcement to investigate 'gender ideology' in schools and prosecute teachers facilitating social transition; Dec 2025 reward memo and May 2026 counterterrorism strategy frame 'radically pro-transgender' ideology alongside violent extremism; 66% poll supports assigned-sex-only documents; division among lowest-support for trans-inclusive policy.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward criteria never list gender ideology; strategy states counterterrorism powers will not target mere disagreement; no national sodomy law, division repealed its sodomy statute in 2019.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both outing probability (heightened scrutiny) and severity by signalling institutional hostility to police and public alike.

minors_guardians.exposure: Division Class C felony for providers giving gender-affirming care under 19; federal order criminalising teachers' facilitation of social transition; national health-rule proposals barring insurance reimbursement under 18; subpoena of under-19 medical records.
minors_guardians.protection: Litigation pending on several youth-focused orders; care ban applies to providers, not the travelling family directly unless care is sought.
minors_guardians.interaction: An adult travelling with a trans minor faces compounded exposure: facility bans in schools/colleges, care refusal, and a felony-layered care regime that deters any medical contact during the visit.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide nondiscrimination or GI coverage in state hate-crime law (1994 statute covers other categories only); only two municipalities offer full protection; state polling among lowest for trans-inclusive policy; ACLU notes wrong-gender daily ID exposes holders to harassment and violence in ID checks.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute (2009) covers gender identity; GI applied to sex under employment law in this circuit since 2011; federal employment nondiscrimination in force.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Weak local recourse plus ID mismatch during police ID checks means street or policing friction has thin division-level remedy, though national hate-crime law applies.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Recurring oversight without remedy: appeals courts upheld surgery-ID requirement and refusal of accurate licences (2024), enforcement allowed of facility bans — institutions enforcing hostile policy; multiple orders enjoined but passport regime in force; no statewide public-accommodations recourse; cited 3.8/100k killing figure is an undercount floor and unusable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Active ACLU litigation on passports, blocked executive orders, running legal-aid FAQ on document rules, national employment and hate-crime protections functioning.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies exist and operate for some claims but the operative record shows courts sustaining the hostile document and facility rules, so recourse mitigates less than paper suggests.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this dossier's rating: 0.35-B features routine, discretionary police stops, passport and phone confiscation, compelled interviews and unofficial files as standing practice against trans visitors. Here entry friction is documented but conditional (discrepancy-triggered refusal, never-automatic fraud findings), there is no documented pattern of routine street stops of trans visitors, and courts plus litigation operate — so this dossier sits above 0.35-B.

Closest fit: routine exposure at checkpoints and services from linked records, a public-order framing of 'deceptive' presentation, documented detention/humiliation and denial of care, narrow anti-discrimination recognition with slow, scarce remedies, inconsistent enforcement. This dossier adds documented immigration-custody abuse (beatings, sexual abuse — severity 4) but lacks 0.45-A's everyday biometric-card exposure; net comparable, marginally lower.

Higher than this dossier: 0.55-C's worst feature is ward placement and partial care denial with ethics committees and ministry complaints available, no custody exposure. This dossier combines passport/visa universal exposure, facility bans with a documented arrest and men's-ward hold, felony-layered youth care, and state-perpetrated custody abuse — broader and more severe, so it rates materially below 0.55-C.

Well above this dossier: 0.75-C has trained respectful border inspection, tribunal appeals with counsel and compensation for unlawful detention, brief detention ending in release. Here the border regime is explicitly restrictive (refusal on sex doubt, lifetime fraud exposure, foreign advisories) and custody carries documented abuse — much worse, so far below 0.75-C.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: a federal document/entry regime that treats sex as a fixed binary (visa refusal on sex doubt, possible lifetime fraud finding, federally funded facility exclusion) interacting with a division imposing birth-certificate bathroom mandates through college, a surgery-gated ID rule sustained by the circuit through 2024, felony liability for under-19 care, and no statewide public-accommodations or state hate-crime recourse. The escalatory chain is documented: document mismatch → secondary screening/referral → immigration custody where trans detainees report beatings, solitary and sexual abuse — hostile policy efficiently enforced, so rule of law does not mitigate. Positives are real but resident-leaning: marriage equality, national employment and hate-crime protections, repealed sodomy law, pending litigation and a legal-aid FAQ. The undercount-floor violence figure is excluded. Net: tier-1 universal exposures with functioning-but-hostile institutions and one documented severity-4 custody pathway — Elevated Risk, upper part.
